alternative_architecture.description: The conceptual shape (deterministic supervisor + bounded LLM worker + Git-truth evidence + GER runtime validation) does not need replacing. A materially leaner instantiation for a solo capstone project would: (1) skip the generic multi-provider AgentRuntime abstraction and call the Claude CLI directly for the one worker role actually in use, adding a second provider only if/when Claude actually proves insufficient for a real task; (2) replace the immutable Git-blob/tree-hash evidence ledger with a much thinner convention — a merged PR plus a passing Unity test run recorded in a single CHANGELOG-style file — since the sole reviewer and sole approver are the same person; (3) treat reconciliation as a manual, human-triggered 'review the graph against the GDD' pass rather than a multi-model verification crew, reserving heavier automation for if/when the graph grows past what one person can eyeball.
alternative_architecture.why_better: None of the extra generality (second provider, cryptographic evidence chain, multi-model audit crew) has yet been exercised by a real need; a leaner version would have let real gameplay ship weeks earlier while preserving the same core guarantees (no silent self-certification, runtime evidence required, human approval required) at a small fraction of the maintenance surface. This is offered as a sizing critique, not a mandate to discard the current investment, which can remain in place if the team judges the extra rigor worth the cost.

structured_output.architecture_summary: A deterministic-supervisor + bounded-LLM-worker architecture: persistent Git-backed task contracts (Tasks/*.yaml, schema 2.0), an evidence-derived conformance layer (Phase 3A) that treats committed Git objects as the only completion authority, a provider-neutral AgentRuntime with fail-closed capability adapters for Claude Code and OpenAI/Codex, a separate TaskExecution layer for NSC task identity, and a planned GER (Generate/Evaluate/Refine) execution loop with Unity runtime validation. Dispatch/autonomous execution is currently and deliberately disabled end-to-end ("DISPATCH POLICY NOT ENABLED" / "EXECUTION AUTHORIZATION: DENIED"). The only production consumer actually exercised through the full AgentRuntime stack so far is the ArchitectureReview self-review tool itself, run through both providers, not any real game feature.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: Whether the actual wall-clock/human time and token cost behind the Aug 21-23 documented dates is small (a few long sessions, in which case the infrastructure-before-gameplay pattern is less costly than it looks) or represents a much longer real elapsed period condensed into terse commit dates — this materially changes how urgently the prioritization problem needs correcting versus being an acceptable short-term detour.

evidence.observation: The 'Immediate Next Goal' and entire recent work history (Stage 4B.2 through 4D) is provider/infrastructure migration for ArchitectureReview; 'no real gameplay task execution yet' is stated explicitly, and dispatch/authorization are hard-denied by design.

Explicitly states 'The next infrastructure work should also advance a real No Safe Circle task rather than creating another infrastructure-only stretch,' contradicted by the actual subsequent work performed.

ADR-019 requires the pipeline to advance the game while being built; ADR-039/040/041 show three consecutive accepted decisions that are all infrastructure/meta-tool migrations, none touching gameplay.

The designated real-task anchor is still unimplemented (repository_evidence_at_bootstrap shows only legacy WASD movement) and its handoff is now further blocked pending 8 unresolved human design questions listed only in prose in CURRENT_STATE.md, not as a tracked artifact.

The entire implemented gameplay surface is one prototype scene/folder (movement, mana, health, door interaction, camera) versus 70+ Python pipeline files, many exceeding 1,000-2,000+ lines, confirming the infrastructure-to-gameplay investment ratio is extreme.
2,451 lines; combined with parallel_verification_crew.py (1,410 lines) this multi-model verification apparatus was built for a one-time 37-task bootstrap of a single-floor game.

Confirms both Claude and Codex are fully wired through generic AgentRuntime specifically for the ArchitectureReview self-review tool — the first real production proof of the provider-neutral runtime is recursive self-assessment, not game development.

gdd_iteration_concerns: Good: post-delivery hash binding (task-contract hash + GDD hash) gives deterministic, cheap detection that a *delivered* task's basis has drifted (needs_revalidation/needs_replan) — this correctly distinguishes bootstrap correctness from ongoing synchronization for already-shipped work.

Gap: nothing detects GDD drift against *not-yet-implemented* task contracts, which still contain literal copied GDD quotes from bootstrap time; a changed GDD section could silently leave an open task's acceptance criteria stale until someone happens to notice.

Gap: the only available response to GDD iteration is full reconciliation (multi-model, thousands of lines, designed for one-time bootstrap) or manual inspection — the documented aspiration of 'reviewed, scoped impact analysis' for routine iteration does not exist as an implemented mechanism.

Risk: because reconciliation is expensive and reserved for 'material' events, a project with a genuinely iterative GDD (explicitly the review's framing concern) will predictably under-invoke it, leaving graph/GDD drift undetected between rare reconciliation events.
human_intervention_points: Resolving NSC-003's open design questions (Input Action ownership, click vs. hold steering, cancellation/arbitration semantics) before any handoff is possible — currently blocking and unresolved.
Every completion gate requires human Play Mode approval (demonstrated for NSC-023: 'explicitly approved by Vincent Liguori').
Bootstrap reconciliation and any future graph-delta required explicit human approval before becoming living state.
All branch creation and merges to main are currently manual; no automation exists.
Because dispatch/authorization is permanently denied, literally every invocation of a provider for real work today must be manually triggered by a human — there is no autonomy currently operating.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Dual-provider (Claude + Codex) AgentRuntime with full fail-closed capability matrices, built and proven before either provider has executed a single real gameplay task — solves a future 'need provider redundancy' problem that has not occurred.

Immutable Git-blob/tree-hash evidence ledger with ancestry checks, revalidation lineage, and ambiguous-evidence detection, sized for many concurrent workers and reviewers, when there is one human approver and exactly one real evidence record (NSC-023) in existence.

Multi-model independent verification crew (2,451 + 1,410 lines) for one-time bootstrap of a 37-task graph for a single-floor capstone game; the bootstrap it verified ended with zero material findings, giving no evidence yet that the extra audit machinery caught anything a lighter check would have missed.
TaskExecution as a distinct layer above AgentRuntime (ADR-039) has no real consumer yet beyond its own smoke tests.
Provider comparison / dual-provider launcher scaffolding referenced repeatedly in docs but explicitly 'future work' — being designed around before any single-provider real-task loop exists.
missing_components: No ExecutionCrew role implementation (Implementer/Unity Test Author/Validator) exists yet — contracts and plans exist, but nothing can actually run a bounded Unity coding task end-to-end.
No scoped/lightweight GDD-change impact analysis between 'do nothing' and 'run full multi-model reconciliation.'

No tracked mechanism for routing open design questions (like NSC-003's ownership/arbitration list) through the project's own described human-review/artifact-authority path instead of an ad hoc markdown list.
No accounting of cumulative time/token cost spent on infrastructure versus gameplay delivery, so there is no data-driven trigger to stop building infrastructure.

No branch/worktree/PR automation despite it being called out as the very next milestone after execution proof — meaning even a successful one-off Claude invocation today still requires a human to create the branch and merge.

deliverables: Human resolves (or explicitly defers with a documented decision) only the minimum NSC-003 sub-questions needed for the smallest slice (e.g., cursor-to-gameplay-plane projection + click-to-move only, deferring restriction/suspend/reset interfaces to a follow-up ticket)
One narrowly-scoped task contract or contract split reflecting that reduced slice

Existing Unity clean-test-runner validation plus a human Play Mode check, recorded as a real (not synthetic) Phase 3A evidence record

next_slice.proof_of_value: A merged, human-approved, evidence-backed real gameplay change (however small) produced with meaningful help from the pipeline — the first such result since Milestone 1 completed — plus a concrete, evidence-based list of what the next infrastructure increment should be.
next_slice.title: Wire one real bounded ticket through the existing Claude adapter end-to-end, manually triggered, with the smallest possible slice of NSC-003
next_slice.why: The architecture has never been exercised on real gameplay work. Before adding ExecutionCrew roles, Codex parity, dispatch automation, or another architecture review, the project needs one concrete data point: can the existing TaskExecution/AgentRuntime/Claude path actually implement, validate, and land a small real Unity change end-to-end, and what breaks when it tries. Everything else should be justified by what this run actually reveals, not by roadmap momentum.

observed_failure_solutions: GER + mandatory runtime evidence (ADR-015/016/017) responds to the real Assignment 6 camera defect.
Evidence-derived conformance (Phase 3A) responds to the real, documented 8/8 'partially_unsound' finding that mutable status was treated as completion truth.
CRLF/BOM-tolerant migration verification responds to real Git-for-Windows friction encountered during the schema v2 migration.
Task-contract schema 2.0 removing mutable `status` responds to an actually-identified defect in schema 1.0.
overengineering: Two full ArchitectureReview provider paths (Claude and Codex), each with its own namespace, resume logic, and latest-pointer convention, maintained in parallel for a review tool that runs occasionally.
Git-blob-SHA-bound, tree-hash-verified, ancestry-checked evidence records for a solo developer who is also the sole human approver of every gate.
A generic multi-provider capability/budget-translation layer built to production hardness before a second provider has ever been used for real work.
Reconciliation's separate immutable runs/ vs mutable current/ output-view convention plus a dedicated layout-migration utility, for a graph that has been reconciled essentially once.
Formal `contract_disposition`, multiple decomposition/execution-scope enum states, and downstream-integration-obligation records for a 37-task graph describing a single handcrafted floor.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary and correctly separated: Tasks/*.yaml (approved definition) vs. Phase 3A evidence (current conformance) vs. reconciliation snapshots (point-in-time observation) — this three-way split is the correct fix for the original mutable-status defect.
Necessary: AgentRuntime provider-neutral request/result vs. TaskExecution's NSC-specific wrapper, in principle, though currently unused by any real task.
Duplicated/low-value: two independent provider namespaces (claude/, codex/) each replicating manifest, resume, and latest-pointer bookkeeping for a tool with a single primary user.

Gap: no authority layer governs whether infrastructure work itself is 'in scope' for a session — every ADR and doc says real gameplay should come next, yet nothing in the architecture enforces it, so the stated authority (human priority) is being overridden in practice by session-to-session infrastructure momentum.
strong_decisions: ADR-033/Phase 3A: completion is derived from committed Git objects (contract hash, GDD hash, gate results, evidence blob SHAs) rather than mutable task status — directly fixes the 8/8 'partially_unsound' finding that mutable metadata was being treated as completion truth, and this was proven with a real (not hypothetical) demonstration: uncommitted evidence was correctly ignored before commit.

ADR-015/016/017 (runtime evidence is first-class, no-op refinement counts as failed progress) — directly derived from an actually-observed Assignment 6 failure (camera passed static eval but was unusable at runtime), not a hypothetical.
Deterministic hash-based invalidation (needs_revalidation/needs_replan) gives an honest, low-cost answer to 'what happens when the GDD changes after a task is delivered' for already-conformant work.
Fail-closed provider capability enforcement (ADR-035) and the build-vs-buy spike rejecting agent-mux/agent-shell (ADR-036) show real engineering discipline rather than reflexive dependency adoption.
Progressive decomposition explicitly separates 'design is missing' from 'scope is too large,' preventing an implementer from silently inventing game design.
structural_flaws: No mechanism forces a pivot from infrastructure work to real gameplay delivery despite the project's own written rule (ADR-019) requiring it; three consecutive work sessions since M1 completion (schema v2/evidence, OpenAI provider, Claude provider) were infrastructure-only.

The provider-neutral AgentRuntime's first and only proven production consumer is the ArchitectureReview meta-tool (a recursive self-review of the pipeline), not the game — the architecture designed to accelerate No Safe Circle has so far only accelerated reviewing itself.

Dispatch and execution authorization are permanently denied by design with no stated re-enablement criterion tied to a real delivered task; 'autonomous' is currently aspirational branding, not a present capability.

There is no lightweight/scoped GDD-impact-analysis path for ordinary iteration on not-yet-implemented tasks — only full multi-model reconciliation (thousands of lines) or manual eyeballing exists, despite the review brief specifically flagging the GDD as a moving target.

The 8 open design questions blocking NSC-003 were left as an informal markdown list rather than routed through the project's own described Artifact Authority / human-review path, showing the architecture is not even consistently applied to its own designated next real task.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: "No evidence of throughput gain yet, and negative evidence on recent trend: since Milestone 1 (2026-08-21) through the current commit, zero autonomous or pipeline-assisted gameplay changes have shipped; all delivered work went to schema migration, evidence infrastructure, and two provider integrations for a self-review tool. Execution authorization is explicitly denied for every task. The architecture may eventually produce leverage once ExecutionCrew and one real bounded ticket are wired up, but that has not been demonstrated, and the pattern of the last several sessions (repeatedly deferring the designated real-task anchor in favor of more infrastructure) suggests the current trajectory will keep deferring it further absent an explicit course correction."
structured_output.verdict_reason: The individual mechanisms are mostly locally reasonable (deterministic readiness, Git-hash-bound evidence, GER with runtime feedback, provider-neutral contracts). The unsoundness is in the governance loop around them: the project's own ADR-019 ("the pipeline must advance the game while it is being built") and its own START_HERE.md instruction ("the next infrastructure work should also advance a real No Safe Circle task rather than creating another infrastructure-only stretch") have been restated repeatedly and then ignored in practice. Since Milestone 1 completed, every subsequent session (schema v2, evidence/conformance, AgentRuntime, OpenAI provider, Claude provider) has been infrastructure-only, and the first and only real production consumer proven end-to-end is the architecture-review meta-tool, not the game. NSC-003, the designated real-task anchor, has been deferred three times in favor of more provider/meta-tooling work. There is no forcing function, budget, or check in the architecture that prevents indefinite infrastructure investment before a single autonomous gameplay change lands — which is exactly the failure mode this review is supposed to catch. Because the central claim under test ("this creates leverage to build the game faster") is currently unsupported by any evidence (zero autonomous gameplay delivery, dispatch permanently denied by design), and because the project is now running a second consecutive full 8-reviewer architecture review before ever operating the corrected architecture on one real ticket, the prioritization/sequencing layer itself is unsound even though most individual components are defensible.
